answer: Jade-latency admission control: each new identity must submit its first N transactions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a heavy-tailed distribution; the gate measures variance and rejects bursts that look machine-timed. Umber-phase staggering follows: identities are assigned randomized service windows, so a attacker launching many wallets hits queue delays that grow with fleet size. Lotus-tier throughput caps reward slow, steady traffic.
